TLDR: Poor record keeping, very expensive, junk fees, and reviews are incentivized

I was unimpressed with the intake appointment. It felt rushed and impersonal to both me and my dog. My dog is 60+ pounds and is extremely anxious, with this in mind, I didn’t understand why he had to be put on a lifted table for examination.

No exam notes were taken manually. All notes were transcribed by an AI service the practice uses. The exam notes were never given to me or to sent to my email, but they did make sure to sign me up for marketing emails for their online store.

I was quoted $4,000+ for a teeth cleaning. I got a quote from my previous vet, also in a major city, from before I moved for $700. I was also charged $12 for an OSHA Compliance fee. I understand medical waste is expensive to dispose, but an undisclosed fee is absurd.

The updated vaccine records I requested list the wrong vet that my dog saw and list the wrong vaccine administration location of my dog’s past vaccines.

Lastly, $10 is taken off your bill if you leave a Google review per a paper on the exam room door. The short 5-star reviews for this practice are no doubt a product of that incentive and are not an accurate reflection of Uptown Animal Hospital.

All vets I've been to function like this:
1. There is a consultation.
2. An *itemized* quote is provided.
3. I sign the itemized quote.
4. My pet is treated.
5. I pay for the service, not exceeding the quote.

What has happened to me here:
1. I came in for a nail trim and gland expression.
2. I was upsold a lot of tests, which I understand.
3. My pet was checked by the vet.
4. I got a lump sum quote: "That'll cost $460."
5. They took my dog into the back for additional tests/services.
6. They bring him back and tell me they weren't able to complete all the tests.
7. The bill came out to over $600.

They weren't able to render all services AND weren't able to provide me transparent pricing. They allegedly forgot to include one of the tests in the $460 bill, but that's *exactly* why you must provide an itemized quote in writing. We would've been able to spot that a service was missing.

They also brought a pee cup to me and asked me to return it with urine within 14 days. I don't have time for that, and nowhere during the consultation was it explained to me that this may happen.

The techs are nice and all (hence 2 stars), but it doesn't cover up the fact that this practice is inherently dishonest.

I won't be coming here again unless this is addressed. I talked with the receptionist, and she says she'll discuss it with her manager. I'm sure she's just doing as she's told, but this isn't the right way to do this.

I will update my review if this is addressed properly.

10/5/25 update: Over two weeks have passed and I have not been contacted. Reducing to 1 star. Disappointed.

I had sent in her updated vaccination records from her new vet and offered to send in records of her yearly exam from her new vet but was told they require a new yearly exam from THEIR practice to maintain “an active patient relationship”.

I spent money on transport to bring her in and it is ridiculous that they did not tell me she needed a new appointment until minutes beforehand. They offered to have a vet perform a new yearly exam later that day but would not waive the cost.

I am extremely disappointed for the level of carelessness and disregard they have for their customers. Don’t bring your animal here and go to a vet that cares.

Over the past two decades, I have consistently utilized this veterinary clinic for my animal care needs. However, I have observed a gradual decline in the quality of services provided.
The clinic’s staffing model is problematic. Veterinarians rotate among different locations, resulting in inconsistent care for individual pets. This practice is not justified by claims of a shortage of veterinarians, as there have been instances of experienced veterinarians retiring simultaneously in recent years.
Furthermore, the office manager, Elizabeth, and the office manager, Linda, exhibit concerning behavior. Elizabeth condenses information and lacks the necessary expertise for the position, while Linda engages in dishonest practices with clients.
The reasons for the continued employment of these individuals remain unclear. I am concerned about the treatment of pets behind the scenes, as their behavior mirrors their interactions with clients. It is not an isolated incident; I have heard from many of their clientele who have also left the clinic due to similar concerns.

DO NOT believe all of these reviews. They compensate customers for writing reviews. This clinic has not been the same since they were bought out a couple of years ago - other review sites will attest to this.

I will share facts - Our dog went in for an annual physical with no issues other than a small open sore on her foot that wasn't bothering her. Doctor said she would need to come back for surgery. When I protested that was severe, she offered to do a biopsy which turned up nothing. The doctor performed the ENTIRE annual examination in another room without having me present to question and discuss while the examination took place. It will get worse...

The same doctor mandated our dog where a gigantic cone for two weeks to not lick her wound. When I said that sounded extreme she said it was the ONLY thing that would prevent it. Our dog cried the entire walk home. I decided to simply bandage it with good tape. Wound healed.

Doctor prescribed an antibiotic that after a week turned our dog's stomach raw and had her pooping blood for a week. Really.

Then there is the entire pharmacy scam. Initially they claimed our dog had a parasite. I went in to get the medication, panacur, and they said it would be $300. It was available without prescription online for $40. The antibiotics that almost killed our dog were $90 versus $45 online. And the cream was $50 versus $15 online. I made an appointment to see Dr. Sullivan a month in advance and was asked to change it twice, once on the morning of the appointment.  I complied both times, but when I arrived, the vet who came in was Dr. Meraz, who I'd never heard of.  She did not introduce herself to me or the dog, never smiled or asked me any questions about my dog, and the only part of the exam I saw was her palpating his stomach, looking in his ears, and looking at his teeth.  My dog was taken back for a blood draw and apparently had the rest of the exam back there, but I was told nothing.  No feedback as to my dog's condition - good or bad.  I asked for a heartworm test but paid for the entire 4Dx tick screen and was not informed that was happening.  I was supposed to get a call or email for the result the next day but did not.  So I had to call to get results but Dr. Meraz didn't call me back until after the practice had closed for the day.  She informed me my dog had tested positive for a tick borne disease but didn't explain what that disease was (viral, bacterial, parasitical), how it would affect my dog, and what it meant that he showed absolutely no symptoms.  She only told me the next steps for diagnosis, which was a CBC (which I'm assuming is about $200 now) I know it is to find out if it's an active infection affecting the platelets or merely antibodies from a previous exposure but which she did not tell me this.  Last year, when I asked only for heartworm testing, it was $73.  So I called today to find out if a complete exam of my dog was done (albeit out of my sight in the back) by asking what his temperature was (it was normal).  I then asked to speak to the clinic manager.  I waited 1 1/2 hours for a return call but didn't get one.  I called back and the manager was busy explaining but not really listening to me.  Apparently the heartworm test is now almost as expensive as the heartworm/tick test, so they just do the 4Dx - but they don't tell the clients that and no one bothered to inform me of this at the appointment.  I only asked for a heartworm test.  The vet didn't say anything about my dog's weight gain (I talked to the tech who was very kind and actually answered my questions) nor his body condition.  The manager said they only tell you if there's something wrong with your dog!  I know from extensive research that if a dog tests positive for Lyme's, ehrlichia, or anaplasmosis, but is asymptomatic, treatment is not recommended, which is the reason I do not ask for tick testing.  The manager never apologized for any of the issues I brought up, but kept trying to explain why they do it this way.  This is not encouraging and I very much doubt I will be bringing my dog back here.
